I'm 45, been farming since I left middle school. My family has about 8 mu of flat land in Quzhou. Every year I do winter wheat followed by summer maize — that's what my father did, that's what all my neighbors do, and it puts food on the table. I don't gamble with new crops.

The wheat went in last October — I planted Shimai 22, an improved variety that doesn't lodge easily. I rotary tilled before sowing and put down base fertilizer then. Right now it's late April and the wheat is at jointing. I've already irrigated once at green-up. The extension fellow says 15 kg nitrogen per mu is enough, but I usually do a bit more — I can't afford a bad year. I'll topdress with urea at jointing, so total nitrogen this season will be about 18 kg per mu. I also put compound fertilizer down at planting, which gives some phosphorus and potassium too. I'll irrigate twice more — now at jointing and again at grain filling if the rain doesn't come — so three times total. I'll spray four times: herbicide once, fungicide once, and insecticide twice because the aphids have been bad lately.

After wheat harvest in early June, I'll plant Denghai 605 hybrid maize immediately. Everyone buys hybrid seed now — you can't save your own. I won't till for maize, just direct seed into the wheat stubble. No-tillage saves diesel and time, and the turnaround between crops is tight. I'll put about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage if the leaves look yellow. That comes to about 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I'll irrigate twice for maize — once after sowing if it's dry, and once at grain filling. Three pesticide sprays: herbicide once and insecticide twice. I expect around 500 kg per mu for wheat and 550 kg per mu for maize. Last year was similar, and I'd rather stick with what I know than try something fancy and lose money.
